 Torino-Monza, Torino chase first hat-trick of wins since 2019 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Torino are playing for more than just another three points against Monza tonight. Ignazio Abate's side have the chance to achieve something they have not managed in the league for quite some time: a third consecutive Serie A win.
 The Granata head into the match after a 2-1 victory over Udinese and an emphatic 3-0 win away at Parma. Those two results have turned the team's form around and could now become a genuine winning streak.
 OneFootball Videos
 Torino have not won three consecutive matches since 2019
 To find the last time Torino won three consecutive games in a single Serie A season, you have to go back to 2019, when Walter Mazzarri was in charge.
 Since then, Toro have put together several short unbeaten runs, but have never managed three straight wins in the same league campaign.
 Against Monza, Abate therefore has the chance to end a seven-year wait and build on the progress shown in recent weeks.
 Ten points from their last five matches
 Torino's upturn in form goes beyond their last two games.
 The Granata have picked up 10 points from their last five league matches , a return that has helped them climb the table quickly and, above all, regain confidence after a difficult start to the season.
 The win over Udinese had already offered encouraging signs. The victory at Parma, with three goals scored and none conceded, added defensive solidity and a clinical edge.
 Monza have never beaten Toro in Serie A
 The head-to-head record also offers an interesting statistic.
 In the six Serie A meetings between Torino and Monza so far, the visitors have never managed to beat the Granata.
 The league record therefore favours Toro, although a very recent encounter serves as a warning against complacency: in September, Monza won 1-0 at the Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino in the Coppa Italia.
 That is a match Abate and his players remember well.
 A match to gauge how much Torino have changed
 Tonight's clash could therefore become a small test of maturity.
 After two consecutive wins, the main challenge will be to maintain that form against a team that caused Toro problems just a few weeks ago.
 Torino go into this match with more confidence than they had back then, though. The 4-4-2 formation is providing greater balance, Simeone has got off the mark with his brace at Parma, Adams is available again and Kulenovic continues to impress.
 Abate wants consistency, not just a result
 For Abate, the historical statistic only matters up to a point. His main concern is to build on the progress made in recent weeks.
 But a third consecutive victory would inevitably carry considerable weight: it would strengthen their league position, further boost the squad's confidence and confirm an upturn compared with the early part of the season.
 Toro have the chance to turn two wins into a genuine winning streak. And to achieve something they have not managed in Serie A since 2019.
